mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months indicates a strengthening of the housing market and overall economic demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the last month suggests an improving labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last month indicates a strengthening of the supply side of the economy, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods analyzed.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it suggests a tightening labor market and potential wage inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over the last quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.
